text:
Authentication uses short-lived bearer tokens issued by the identity service. Tokens expire after fifteen minutes and must be refreshed using the rotating refresh token.

Error code XR-4471 indicates a failed authentication handshake. The usual cause is a client secret that was rotated on the server but not updated in the client configuration.

Error code XR-4472 is returned when the token audience does not match the requested resource server. Check the audience claim before opening a ticket.

Invoices are generated on the first business day of each month and cover the previous billing period. Usage is metered hourly and aggregated nightly.

Prorated charges apply when a plan changes mid-cycle. The proration is calculated from the effective timestamp of the plan change, not from the start of the day.

Refunds are issued to the original payment method and typically settle within five to ten business days.

The public API enforces a rate limit of one thousand requests per minute per organization. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

Batch endpoints count each item in the payload as a separate request against the quota. A batch of fifty items therefore consumes fifty units.

Rate limits can be raised on enterprise plans by contacting support with the expected peak throughput.

Deployments are immutable. Each release builds a new container image tagged with the commit SHA and promotes it through staging before production.

Rollback is performed by re-pointing the production alias at the previous image tag. No rebuild is required and the operation completes in under thirty seconds.

Database migrations run as a separate job before the new image receives traffic. Migrations must be backward compatible with the previous release.

Objects are stored with server-side encryption enabled by default using keys managed by the platform. Customer-managed keys are available on request.

Lifecycle policies move objects to cold storage after ninety days of inactivity and delete them after seven years unless a legal hold is applied.

Versioning is enabled on all buckets. Deleting an object writes a delete marker rather than removing the underlying data.

Webhook deliveries are retried with exponential backoff for up to twenty-four hours. Each attempt carries the same idempotency key so receivers can deduplicate.

A webhook endpoint is disabled automatically after seven consecutive days of failures. Re-enable it from the dashboard once the receiver is healthy.

Signatures are computed with HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body. Verify the signature before parsing the payload.

Single sign-on supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Just-in-time provisioning creates the user account on first successful login.

Error code SSO-8802 means the assertion was signed with a certificate that is not in the trust store. Upload the current signing certificate in the identity provider settings.

Group membership is synchronized on each login. Removing a user from a mapped group revokes their access at the next authentication.

The search index is rebuilt incrementally every five minutes. Newly created records become searchable within one indexing cycle.

Queries support boolean operators, phrase matching with double quotes, and field-scoped filters using the field:value syntax.

Deleted records are removed from the index immediately rather than waiting for the next rebuild.

Data exports run asynchronously and produce a signed download URL that remains valid for one hour. Large exports are split into multiple compressed parts.

Exports include all records visible to the requesting user at the moment the job starts. Records created after that point are not included.

The export format is newline-delimited JSON. A manifest file lists every part with its checksum.

Audit logs capture every write operation with the actor, timestamp, source address and the affected resource identifier. Read operations are not logged by default.

Logs are retained for four hundred days and can be streamed to an external SIEM over a secure syslog endpoint.

Audit entries are immutable. Corrections are recorded as new entries rather than edits to existing ones.

Outbound traffic originates from a fixed set of published IP ranges. Add these ranges to an allowlist when the receiving system enforces network restrictions.

All connections require TLS 1.2 or higher. Cipher suites without forward secrecy are rejected during the handshake.

Private connectivity over a dedicated peering link is available on enterprise plans.

Each organization may create up to five hundred projects. Archived projects do not count toward the limit.

A single project supports up to fifty concurrent background jobs. Jobs beyond that queue in submission order.

Storage quota is enforced per organization rather than per project, so one project can consume the entire allocation.
